questions.question: May tickets remain unassigned (including existing and new tickets), or must every ticket have an owner?
questions.options: Allow unassigned tickets, preserving a visible unassigned state and permitting ownership to be cleared / require every ticket to have an owner, preventing creation or clearing without a valid owner.

questions.question: Should owners come from the fixed local roster Avery Stone (avery-stone) and Jordan Lee (jordan-lee), or be entered as free text?
questions.options: Use the fixed local roster for consistent identities and controlled validation / accept free text for flexibility, with greater risk of inconsistent names and matching.

questions.question: Is displaying ownership sufficient, or should the queue also filter by owner in combination with existing search, status, and priority filters?
questions.options: Display ownership without adding a filter for the smaller change / add an owner filter that intersects with search, status, and priority for stronger queue discovery.

questions.question: If every ticket must have an owner, how should existing ownerless tickets be handled during migration?
questions.options: Backfill a Human-selected default owner for all existing tickets / require an explicit migration mapping for existing tickets / retain existing tickets as unassigned exceptions while requiring ownership for new and subsequently edited tickets; each option trades migration simplicity against attribution accuracy and policy consistency.

fields.Outcome: Ownership is optional. Existing and newly created tickets start unassigned; assignment, reassignment and clearing are supported on ticket detail, not on the creation form. Keep all existing ticket identifiers, values and timestamps unchanged during migration.
fields.Rationale: This bounded development rehearsal must preserve existing intake and legacy data; responsibility is assigned after triage rather than invented during migration.

/sdlc decide spec v1 Q-1
Outcome: Ownership is optional. Existing and newly created tickets start unassigned; assignment, reassignment and clearing are supported on ticket detail, not on the creation form. Keep all existing ticket identifiers, values and timestamps unchanged during migration.
Rationale: This bounded development rehearsal must preserve existing intake and legacy data; responsibility is assigned after triage rather than invented during migration.

fields.Outcome: Use only the local roster Avery Stone (avery-stone) and Jordan Lee (jordan-lee), plus Unassigned. Empty ownership form input normalizes to database null. Reject forged nonempty owner values and nonexistent ticket IDs explicitly without mutating any row; an already-current owner is a write-free successful no-op preserving updatedAt. A real change updates only ownership and a nondecreasing updatedAt.
fields.Rationale: Fixed identities keep this small demonstration deterministic without authentication or external directories, while server and storage validation preserve existing records.

fields.Outcome: Include an owner filter with All owners, Unassigned, Avery Stone and Jordan Lee, intersecting existing search/status/priority filters. For AC-3 assign INC-0001 and INC-0003 to Avery, INC-0002 to Jordan, and leave INC-0004 unassigned: All returns 4, Avery returns exactly {0001,0003}, Jordan {0002}, and Unassigned {0004}; Avery+open+high+inc-1 returns only 0001, and Avery+critical returns none. Clearing only owner means All owners while preserving the other filter selections; summary cards remain unfiltered and navigation must not display a stale owner selection.
fields.Rationale: Visible responsibility alone does not help agents find their work; exact result sets and preserved filter state make the intended behavior objectively testable.

Migrate existing tickets to null/Unassigned with no default owner or attribution mapping, preserve every pre-existing field and timestamp exactly, and keep all four fixed scenario fixtures and initial summary counts unchanged. intentSnapshot.title: [Development rehearsal] Discover and deliver ticket ownership
intentSnapshot.body:
Delivery Execution: development-test

This is an explicitly authorized scripted development rehearsal using the
repository owner's account. It is not independent Human review, genuine Human
acceptance, or evidence of three completed live scenarios. Use the actual
version-bound decision commands; do not infer approval from this statement.

## Problem or opportunity

The existing IT service desk under demos/it-service-desk can create, search,
and update tickets, but has no owner field. During the simulated support-team
handoff, agents cannot see who is responsible or identify unassigned work.
The source baseline demonstrates the missing capability. We have no customer
interviews, measured business baseline, or verified productivity claims.

## Proposed outcome

Make responsibility visible on the queue and ticket detail, support a simple
ownership handoff, and preserve existing tickets and workflows. Evaluate the
result using observable application behavior, exact fixture result sets, and
data preservation, not invented business metrics. Alternatives include keeping
the current process or adding only visibility without filtering.

## Affected users and systems

Support agents and team leads using the existing SQLite-backed IT service desk.
The fixture people and tickets are synthetic demonstration data.

## Constraints and non-goals

Keep a small brownfield change. Preserve ticket identifiers, existing values
and timestamps during migration, and preserve create/status/search/summary
behavior. Use labeled keyboard-usable controls, explicit invalid-input errors,
and persisted behavior after restarting the same container/volume.

Do not add authentication, external identity integration, notifications, SLAs,
bulk assignment, free-text audit history, or unrelated dashboards.

The existing ownership scenario manifest and acceptance checklist are candidate
demo fixtures and observable checks, not a substitute for answering the policy
questions below. After those decisions, retain AC-1 through AC-5 for migration,
assignment/reassignment/clearing, exact filter intersections, accessibility and
invalid-input preservation, and unchanged ticket creation/status behavior.
Do not copy implementation from the previously completed demo repository.

## Open questions

Register these three policy choices as blocking discovery questions; do not
silently decide them from candidate fixtures or older example documents:

1. May tickets remain unassigned (including existing and new tickets), or must
   every ticket have an owner?
2. Should owners come from the fixed local roster Avery Stone (avery-stone)
   and Jordan Lee (jordan-lee), or be entered as free text?
3. Is displaying ownership sufficient, or should the queue also filter by
   owner in combination with existing search, status, and priority filters?

Additional consequential ambiguities should be made explicit rather than
inventing decisions. AI proposes the Spec; only recorded decisions followed
by explicit approval authorize advancement.
